mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen each of the last three weeks (-23.4 to -12.4), indicating a steady return to in-person work. This commuting recovery mechanically increases weekday foot traffic near offices and transit hubs, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -23.4 to -12.4 over 3 weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean fails to rise despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend for the full horizon, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops sharply week-on-week (a proxy for renewed public caution or restrictions tied to emerging variant concern), this signals impending policy tightening or self-imposed avoidance that will suppress discretionary RETAIL_REC visits over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week to below -25%
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has ranged between -18.6 and -22.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses the -25% threshold but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not decline relative to the prior 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A joint pattern of rising PARKS mobility and falling RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates households are substituting at-home time for outdoor and errand-based activity. This combined behavioral shift increases overall willingness to leave home, which spills over into higher RETAIL_REC visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -20.1 to -13.9 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.9 to 7.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: If PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL falls concurrently for two weeks but RETAIL_REC's mean does not increase over the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The decision date falls in mid-December, within the peak holiday shopping window. Regardless of other mobility categories, seasonal consumer demand for gift and holiday purchases produces a short-term uptick in RETAIL_REC over the next week independent of other series' trajectories.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-12-15, within holiday shopping season
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's mean over the next week is not higher than the current week's mean despite the holiday period, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility sustains a recovery above -10% for two consecutive weeks, it signals a durable return-to-office regime that drives consistent weekday retail and recreation visits in commercial districts, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES exceeds -10% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -12.4 in the latest week, approaching the -10% threshold
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES crosses above -10% for two weeks but RETAIL_REC's mean does not rise over the subsequent two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained stable and mildly positive (0.6 to 3.1) across all four weeks, reflecting consistent essential-trip behavior unaffected by discretionary mobility swings. This stability indicates no behavioral disruption to baseline shopping patterns, implying RETAIL_REC will not systematically shift beyond recent noise over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged narrowly between 0.0 and 3.1 across four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains stable within its historical band but RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean shows a large directional move (beyond +/-3 points), the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES alongside a rise in RESIDENTIAL would jointly indicate renewed public-health caution or policy-driven restriction, compounding to suppress RETAIL_REC more severely than any single series would predict alone, over a four-week horizon.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series show partial recovery trends that could reverse together
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline while RESIDENTIAL rises concurrently for two weeks but RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean does not fall, the hypothesis is rejected.

When PARKS falls below -20%, cold-weather displacement shifts recreational activity indoors toward retail venues, producing a short-term rise in RETAIL_REC within one week.
